title: Narrow TensorView prefix selectors without full entry scans
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView.select() validated selectors against canonical axes but rebuilt an axis-name map on every call and then linearly scanned the entire retained sparse-entry tuple even when selectors fixed the leading coordinate axes. select() with no selectors also rebuilt an equal result tuple instead of reusing the immutable retained tuple.
primary_claim: TensorView.select() now reuses the canonical sorted axis and entry orders. Empty selection returns the immutable retained entries tuple directly. Selectors that bind a contiguous leading axis prefix use bisect_left/bisect_right to bound the candidate interval before applying the existing exact predicate; non-prefix selectors retain the prior exact filtering semantics and fail-closed validation.
gardener_decision: Exploit ordering already owned by TensorView rather than adding an entry index, selector cache, lookup service, alternate sparse representation or planner. Preserve full filtering for selectors that cannot be narrowed by the current canonical leading-axis order.
acceptance: select() with no coordinates reuses the immutable retained entries tuple instead of rematerializing it
selector axis lookup reuses canonical sorted TensorView axes rather than materializing a full per-call axis-name map
a selector over the leading canonical axis bounds the candidate entry interval with binary search before exact filtering
an adversarial 512-entry probe refuses linear iteration or slicing and caps integer entry reads at 28 while selecting the final two-entry prefix
non-prefix selectors preserve exact filtering semantics
unknown axes and undeclared labels continue to fail closed
